hints: Focus on what isomer really means here, same molecular formula but different arrangement of atoms.
Count the total carbons in each name, remembering that methyl branches add extra carbons to the main chain.
Look for the pair where both alcohols add up to the same total number of carbons, so both have the same formula $C_xH_{2x+2}O$.
walkthrough:
**Recall what alcohol isomers need**

Isomers must have the same molecular formula. For an alcohol, that means the same total number of carbons, hydrogens and one oxygen.

General formula for a saturated alcohol:
$$C_xH_{2x+2}O$$

**Count carbons in each alcohol**

The parent chain gives the base number, then add any methyl branches. Let's list them simply.

$butan\text{-}1\text{-}ol = 4 \text{ carbons, so } C_4H_{10}O$

$2,2\text{-}dimethylpropan\text{-}1\text{-}ol = 3 + 2 = 5 \text{ carbons, so } C_5H_{12}O$

$butan\text{-}2\text{-}ol = 4 \text{ carbons, so } C_4H_{10}O$

$2\text{-}methylpropan\text{-}2\text{-}ol = 3 + 1 = 4 \text{ carbons, so } C_4H_{10}O$

$pentan\text{-}1\text{-}ol = 5 \text{ carbons, so } C_5H_{12}O$

$propan\text{-}2\text{-}ol = 3 \text{ carbons, so } C_3H_8O$

**Match the pair with identical formulas**

Only one pair both have 4 carbons and formula $C_4H_{10}O$. They differ in structure, one is a straight chain with OH on carbon 2, the other is branched with OH on a tertiary carbon.

That is the isomeric pair, so that is the answer.

options.A: Incorrect. Butan-1-ol is $C_4H_{10}O$ but 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol is $C_5H_{12}O$ (3 from propane plus 2 methyls). Different formulas, so they cannot be isomers.
options.B: Correct. Butan-2-ol is $C_4H_{10}O$ and 2-methylpropan-2-ol is also $C_4H_{10}O$ (3 from propane plus 1 methyl). Same formula with different carbon skeleton and position of OH, so they are structural isomers.
options.C: Incorrect. Pentan-1-ol is $C_5H_{12}O$ but 2-methylpropan-2-ol is $C_4H_{10}O$. The carbon counts differ, so they are not isomers. This traps students who focus on the -ol ending and ignore chain length.
options.D: Incorrect. Propan-2-ol is $C_3H_8O$ but 2-methylpropan-2-ol is $C_4H_{10}O$. They are both secondary/tertiary alcohols with similar names, but different molecular formulas, so not isomers.
